_extract.root_split_contract_note: A composition permits exactly one ingredient. The compatibility root retains the Support pin its task Source requires, and since 2026-08-03 it retains ONLY Support operations: the nine legacy Help Center reads moved to the zendesk-help-center sibling, pinned to the official Help Center contract that actually documents them. The earlier arrangement kept them on the Support pin and relied on this fixture to vouch for them, which meant they could never clear the publish op-prover; splitting them satisfies the one-ingredient constraint without asking the fixture to stand in for a proof. They are NOT duplicates of the Help Center leaf packs — all nine are the no-locale read forms, verified route-by-route as absent from both leaves.

source_decision.reason: The hash-pinned Support list/read contracts expose the declared identity, update time, task projection, and bounded cursor continuation. The Source remains read-only and filtered with no tombstone claim.

exclusions.reason: The official endpoint requires multipart/form-data, but the Help Center OpenAPI operation omits its request-body contract. The REST binding has no multipart encoder or request-side file_ref transport, so JSON or an empty request would be non-executable.

The official endpoint requires multipart/form-data, but the Help Center OpenAPI operation omits its request-body contract. The REST binding has no multipart encoder or request-side file_ref transport, so JSON or an empty request would be non-executable.

The route returns the current session CSRF token. That token is session authority rather than Help Center business data, so exposing it as an ordinary recipe result would leak a credential owned by connection and session handling.
The official contract exposes no request body or parameter schema for the new password. A generated operation would send no credential and cannot truthfully execute the documented action.
OAuth clients, secrets, and tokens belong to connection enrollment and revocation. Exposing them as ordinary recipe arguments or results would leak or destroy connection authority.

The `api_token` object in these responses carries a `token` field — the usable Zendesk API token. Returning it in an ordinary operation result makes the result a secret channel, and the list route hands back every token at once. Token lifecycle belongs to connection enrollment, not to recipe arguments and results.

The official prose requires raw file bytes, but the OpenAPI operation has no request schema. The REST binding has no binary request or request-side file_ref transport, so a generated empty or JSON request would be non-executable.
